content_md:
I randomly spotted a book a while back at a bookstore whose title immediately appealed to me: *Leaders Eat Last* by Simon Sinek,  Sometimes there’s a thesis in a title that immediately resonates. This is one of those. So I got it from the library and started reading it, but couldn’t get past the first chapter. It’s been a long time since I read an actual airport type business book and I guess I’d forgotten how cloying the genre is. Not a criticism of the book itself, especially since I didn’t read much of it. And I guess it’s what sells. But damn it’s hard to read. The airbrushed anecdotes with heartfelt quotes, the sincere affective rhetoric, with motivational exhortations poured on thick. And very little of the depth I thought I might get. It felt like the title said it all.

Since I’ve been reading so many dense history books lately, it felt like eating greasy, processed fast food after several days of eating healthy. 

Now I want to read a “real” book with this title.
